messages:
maria: Heads-up — we've seen a spike in GPU pod evictions in eu-west1c over the last 30m. Noticed it correlates with a surge of short-seq inference jobs + a few large-seq training batches landing on the same racks. Eviction rate ~3x normal.
kevin: Any errors in kube-scheduler logs or node-level OOM/thermal events?
maria: scheduler logs show a lot of 'failedFit' for tiny pods because of 'gpu-count' but also 'affinityMismatch' even though labels look fine. Node metrics show NVLINK peer queues spiking on a subset of hosts (rack-12).
bjorn: Could be placement heuristic is trying to preserve NVLINK locality for large-seq jobs and leaving tiny pods scattered, causing fragmentation. Have we tried soft-affinity to co-locate tiny pods into warm pools?
maria: We already have warm pools but the warm-pool controller is refusing some candidates due to seq_length_estimate tag (new heuristic we rolled last week). That may be the delta.
carmen: timeline: deploy 17:02 updated seqlen-aware scoring, 17:18 we saw first evictions, 17:40 rollout completed for scheduler-svc. Matches.
kevin: Can you paste a snippet of the scheduler scoring decision for one of the failures?
maria: Sure — from scheduler debug: 
```
candidate node: node-eu-west1c-r12-07
scores: [resourceScore=60, localityScore=95, seqlenPenalty= -40]
finalScore=115 (threshold 120)
rejectedReason: finalScore below threshold -> preempt attempt
```
kevin: seqlenPenalty is new. That -40 looks harsh. It may be blocking tiny pods from filling gaps.
bjorn: If seqlenPenalty prefers NVLINK-coalesced placement for predicted long sequences, we might be forcing large jobs into racks and leaving stranded single-slot fragments elsewhere. That increases overall fragmentation and then preempt cycles.
maria: Agree. Metrics show packing density dropped on rack-09/-10 while rack-12 hosts beefed up. Evictions are mostly for pods requesting 0.125 GPUs.
carmen: Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback seqlen-aware scoring 2) soften penalty 3) allow tiny-pod override for warm-pool candidates. Which is least risky?
kevin: Easiest is to reduce the penalty value and push a canary. Rollback if no improvement in 10m.
bjorn: Also consider adding a small negative weight for nvlink-locality on <0.5 GPU requests. That lets tiny pods fill small slots regardless of NVLINK.
maria: I'll open a canary PR to change seqlenPenalty from -40 -> -8 and add override for warm-pool membership.
scheduler-bot: deploy triggered: sched-config-canary -> image:sched:v2026.03.21-canary (rollout started) :rocket:
maria: Can we watch replica eviction count and packing density heatmap? Links: metrics/gpu/evictions?range=30m and heatmaps/packing?rack=eu-west1c
kevin: Watching — eviction spike dropping in the first 3 minutes. Packing density on rack-09 rising slowly.
carmen: If canary behaves, promote to 50% lanes. Also audit any tenant-level seqlen tags — some clients send wildly incorrect estimates.
bjorn: Long term: we should add a post-deploy evaluation for placement heuristics that measures fragmentation and evict-rate for 1h after rollout. This would've caught it before full flip.
maria: Agreed. For now canary -> 20% then 100% if stable. Rolling back plan ready.
kevin: 👍 keep me posted. If evictions trend back to baseline in 15m let's promote.
maria: Update 1790004360: evictions down ~65%, warm-pool fill improved. Rolling to 20% now.
carmen: Nice. Filing follow-up ticket to add fragmentation metric and origin-trace for seqlen tags.
maria: Thanks all :thumbsup:
